EDUDELIGHT GROUP OF SCHOOLS
1 BENSON AVENUE, LEKKI PHASE 1, LAGOS
STATE.
3RD
TERM EXAMINATION 2019/2020 SESSION
SUBJECT:    BASIC SCIENCE                                                            CLASS:  J.S.S 1
Section A:  Objectives
- The ability of a living thing to respond
to external stimuli is (a) respiration
(b) irritability  (c)
excretion  (d) growth
- Another name for womb is  (a) cervix
(b) hymen  (c) clitoris  (d) uterus
- One of these is a source of protein (a)
Egg  (b) yam  (c) butter
(d) fruit
- Water is made up of  (a) carbon and oxygen  (b) hydrogen and oxygen  (c) carbon and hydrogen (d) hydrogen and
nitrogen
- _________is the ability to pass out waste
products  (a) irritability  (b) excretion                         (c) reproduction  (d) movement
- Abestor and cement are responsible for
______pollution  (a) water  (b) land
(c) Air  (d)Noise
- One of these is an example of
non-renewable energy  (a) petrol  (b) water
(c) sun  (d) wind
- One of these is not an example of
S.T.I  (a) gonorrhea    (b) Chlamydia  (c) Ebola (d)Syphilis
- Energy due to motion is  (a) electrical energy  (b) potential
(c) solar energy (d) kinetic energy
- In radio, electrical energy is convert to
_______energy  (a) light  (b) sound
(c) mechanical  (d)potential
- The release of matured ovum from the ovary
in female is ____(a) menstruation                       (b) conception  (c) ovulation
(d) zygote
- All of these are force field EXCEPT  (a) magnetic force  (b) tension
(c) gravitational force  (d)electric
force
- All these are microscopic organisms
EXCEPT  (a) spider  (b) bacteria
(c) virus  (d)fungi
- The energy conversion that involves in
rubbing of your palms is ______(a) mechanical energy to sound energy  (b) heat energy to sound energy  (c) mechanical energy to heat               (d) sound energy to heat energy
- Lack of vitamin D leads to _______(a)
kwashiorkor  (b) beriberi  (c) ricket
(d) sterility
Section B:  Fill in the gaps
- The force that opposes motion is
_____________________
- An object thrown up tends to fall to the
ground due to _________force
- ________________occurs where the released
sperm and ovum is implanted in the uterine wall.
- The reproductive organ that produces and
releases mature eggs is ___________________
- When the earth comes between the sun and
the moon is called _____________________
Section
C:  Theory (Attempt four questions from
this section)
1a.       Explain
space travel
b.         What are the four regions of
atmosphere?
c.         State 2 benefits and 2 dangers of space
travel
d.         What is gravity?
2.         Mention 3 effects of gravitation on
objects
b.         What is satellite?
c.         Mention 3 types of satellites and give
one use each.
3a.       What is teenage pregnancy?
b.         Mention 3 implications of teenage
pregnancy
c.         Mention 3 people that can help a
pregnant teenager
d.         List 3 implications of taking drug
without doctor’s prescription in pregnancy
4.         Calcualte the work done when an object
7kg was raised to a height 10 metres.
Force of gravity is 9.8mS2
b.         Differntiate between gravitational
force and magnetic force.
c.         Explain the importance of frction
d.         State the unit of the following
(i)         force                (ii)        work
5a.       Explain the stages of growth and
development of foetus
b.         Identify the components of the solar
system.
c.         Explain the following terms
(i)         eclipse of the sun,
(ii)       eclipse of the moon
(iii)      season

EDUDELIGHT GROUP OF SCHOOLS
1 BENSON AVENUE, LEKKI PHASE 1, LAGOS
STATE.
3RD  TERM EXAMINATION 2019/2020 SESSION
SUBJECT:    BASIC SCIENCE                                                  CLASS:  J.S.S 2
Section A:  Objectives
- One of these is permanent change in
development  (a) menstruation in
female  (b) obesity  (c)menopause
(d) malnutrition
- All of these are factors that influence
growth and development except  (a)
hormone  (b)heredity  (c) nutrition
(d) size
- The S.I unit for power is (a) joules  (b) watts
(c) Newton  (d) metre per secs.
- Calculate the work done, if a force of 14N
is used to drag a box through a distance of 5m
(a) 35J  (b) 70J  (c) 700J
(d) 350J
- The stored food in our bodies possess
_______energy  (a) chemical  (b) kinetic
(c) potential (d) solar
- If a boy of mass 50kg drags a box through
a distance of 10m.  How much work is
done?       (a) 50KJ,  (b) 5KJ
(c) 500KJ  (d) 5000KJ
- What part of the fish enables it to swim
in water?  (a) gills  (b) stream line body  (c) nose
(d) tail
- Animal that eats another animals is  (a) prey
(b) parasite  (c) predator  (d) nematode
- Desert is an example of ______habitat  (a) aquatic
(b) terrestrial  (c) ax
boreal  (d) salt water
- All of these are factors that affect
evaporation except  (a) pressure  (b) the temperature of the liquid  (c) the size of the liquid  (d) the nature of the liquid.
- The energy change involved when a torch
battery is connected to a bulb is  (a)
light energy to mechanical energy  (b)
chemical energy to light energy  (c)
potential energy to heat energy  (d)
chemical energy to heat energy
- The method of heat transfer in liquid
is  (a) conduction  (b) condensation  (c) convection  (d) radiation
- When someone has had sexual intercourse
before, makes a decision to abstain from sex until later in life is _____abstinence   (a) delayed
(b) life long  (c) periodic  (d) secondary
- Agrochemical is used by  (a) pharmacists  (b) cosmetologist   (c) farmers
(d) painters.
- One of these is used to make petroleum
jelly  (a) diesel oil  (b) natural gas  (c) lubricating oil wax  (d) bitumen
Section B:  Fill in the gap
- The method through which heat is
transferred through space is ________________
- ____________is a method of drug use
- A thick dark viscous liquid is
_______________________
- ____________is used to make protective coatings
for road surfaces
- HIV can be transmitted to baby from the
mother through ____________________
Section C: Theory
(Answer four questions from this section)
1a.       What is heat flow?
b.         List 2 insulators
c.         Explain the three methods of heat
transfer
d.         Give one illustration of one of the
method.
2a.       Mention 2 importance each of breast
feeding to the mother and baby.
b.         Mention 2 prevention of HIV
c.         Explain abstinence
d.         Explain the four types of abstinence
3a.       Give 2 reason why adolescents engage in premarital
sex?
b.         Who do you need to abstain from
premarital sex?  Give 2 reasons
c.         Define chemical
d.         Explain the classes of chemical
4a.       State 3 safety measures when using
chemicals
b.         Mention 3 methods of drug abuse
c.         Explain 2 social risk factors in drug
abuse
5a.       Explain crude oil refining
b.         State 3 products of a typical
fractional distillation of crude oil and their uses
c.         Mention 3 states in Nigeria where oil
refineries are located.
d.         Enumerate the importance of crude oil
and petrochemicals to Nigeria.

STATE.
3RD  TERM EXAMINATION 2019/2020 SESSION
SUBJECT:    BASIC SCIENCE                                                CLASS:  J.S.S 3
Section A:  Objectives
- The three states of matter are (a) atom,
electron and proton  (b) gas vapour and
solid             (c) gas, liquid and
solid  (d) solid, water and gas
- The part of the eye on which image of an
object is formed is called the  (a)
cornea  (b) iris  (c) lens
(d) retina
- Which of the following is an electric
conductor?  (a) cloth  (b)
copper  (c) glass (d) plastic
- The muscles in the upper arm are called
(a) biceps and forceps  (b) biceps and
triceps                (c) tibia and
fibula (d) tibia and biceps
- Which of the following metals is the least
reactive in the activity series?  (a)
Ca  (b) Cu             (c) K  (d) Mg
- Which of the following is not a
metal?  (a) zinc  (b) calcium
(c) carbon  (d) sodium
- Which of the following vitamins if
deficient leads to sterility?  (a) B  (b) C
(c) D  (d) E
- The circulatory system of the human body
carries mainly  (a) fats and oil  (b) blood                            (c) hemoglobin  (d) water
- The total number of atoms in four
molecules of hydrogen is  (a) 2  (b) 8
(c) 12  (d) 6
- Which of these is respiratory
disease?  (a) asthma  (b)chicken pox  (c) cholera
(d)typhoid
- Which of these particles make up the
nucleus of an atom  (a) electrons and
neutrons  (b)neutrons and protons  (c) protons
(d) electrons and protons
- Which of these is a gland?  (a) spinal cord  (b) pituitary
(c) cerebellum  (d) olfactory
lobes
- The following are parts of the brain
except  (a) cerebellum  (b) cerebrum
(c) olfactory lobes  (d) spinal
cord
- Which of the following compound is called
trioxinitrate  (v) acid?  (a) HCI
(b) HNO3
(c) H2 SO4
(d) NaNO3
- The reactioin between a base and an acid
is generally described as  (a)
reduction                   (b)
neutralization  (c) corrosion  (d) hydrolysis.
Section B:  Fill in the Gaps
- The process of heat transfer in an iron
rod is known as ______________________
- The chemical name for common salt is
_____________________________
- The male sex cell is _________________
- The formula for Hydrogen tetraoxo sulphate
(vi) is ___________________
- The body frame work of the human body is
referred to as ________________system
Section C
(Theory):  Answer 4 questions from this
section
1a.       What is an acid?
b.         List 3 properties of an acid
c.         Give the formula of the following
(i)         Hydrochloric acid
(ii)        Sodium chloride
d.         What is P.H of a substance?
e.
Solution
i
ii
iii
iv
v
P.H
values
2
3
5
7
10
i.          Which of the above solution is most
basic?
ii.         Which one is likely to be water?
2a.       What
do you understand by the term
(i)         Atomic
number  (ii) Mass number?
b.         List
3 media through which sound travels
c.         Define
echo
d.         Define
the following terms:
(i) (a) Transparent object  (b) Opaque object
e.         State
the mode of transfer of heat in the following
(i)         sun
(ii) water
3.         Define
radioactivity
b.         Mention
the 3 types of radiation, the symbols and one property each
c.         State
2 uses of radioactivity
d.         Mention
1 danger of radioactivity
4a.       What
is weather?
b.         List
3 types of weather
c.         State
3 factors that affect the weather condition
d.         Mention
3 radioactive elements.
5a.       Mention 3 consequences of deforestation
b.         What are the four layers of the
atmosphere?
c.         Explain gravity
d.         Mention 2 benefits of space.
